text:
maria: Onboarded silica9b-v2 (int4, per-channel symmetric) to canary last night. Perf bench looked fine, but in canary traffic we're seeing intermittent OOMs and "slab jitter" tail failures when requests hit batching+slowgen combos.
sam: Ugh. Can you paste the canary config and a recent OOM log? Any pattern for prompt length / max_new_tokens? :thinking_face:
maria: latest route config:
```
model: silica9b-v2
batching:
  batch_size: 8
  batch_window_ms: 12
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 512
  prefetch: true
  soft_reserve: 0.3
```
OOM snippet (from runtime):
```
E2026-03-23 02:12:14.123 runtime.cpp:452] AllocFailed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory) attempting 1.2 GiB
E2026-03-23 02:12:14.124 runtime.cpp:455] slab_free_list: low-water trigger hit, fragmentation 0.48
E2026-03-23 02:12:14.124 runtime.cpp:456] last-op: kv_prefetch + continuous_batch commit
```
li: Two quick hypotheses:
1) High max_new_tokens (512) + prefetch populates large KV for long sequences -> fragmentation under micro-bursts.
2) Batch pacing + slowgen causes tail requests to hold buffers longer, increasing slab churn.
noah: Agreed. For a short mitigation we should lower defaults on the model and add an eviction/trim tweak. Proposed immediate changes (canary patch):
- reduce max_new_tokens to 128
- set batch_window_ms -> 6 (narrower window to reduce concurrent KV growth)
- disable prefetch for this model
- soft_reserve -> 0.2
- enable kv_eviction_threshold: 0.75
maria: Sounds good. Quick command to apply to the canary route:
```
# apply model defaults for canary
redwoodctl models update --model silica9b-v2 --env canary --set "defaults.max_new_tokens=128" --set "defaults.prefetch=false" --set "batching.batch_window_ms=6" --set "defaults.soft_reserve=0.2"
```
sam: Also add a short-term runtime patch: lower slab freelist high-water mark and enable 'slot_compactor' for the canary pool. I'll open infra patch and push to canary nodes.
li: For longer term: we should run a quant-sensitivity eval comparing int4 per-channel symmetric -> int8 hybrid for silica9b-v2. If int4's allocation patterns are causing fragmentation due to kernel memory layout, int8 might smooth allocations.
maria: I'll kick off an eval run: dataset = 2k short+long prompts, measure 99/99.9 latency, OOM rate, and token-efficiency. Want to try auto-batching profile as well.
noah: +1. When you run the eval, include a max_new_tokens sweep [64,128,256] and batch_size sweep [2,4,8]. We'll link results to the rollout checklist.
deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/infra/slot-compactor-v0.3 -> canary (3 nodes). Will post status updates.
maria: Thanks. For tracking: I'll lower canary traffic to 5% until we validate. Plan: apply defaults now, watch for 10m, then run eval and decide rollout.
sam: ping me if OOMs persist after defaults change; I'll roll a kernel fallback to int8 on a per-node basis as emergency fallback. :thumbsup:
maria: applying now -> will report in 10m. Thanks all :rocket:
